content: I said: Hey chat, good to see you — settle in, we're building something today, I just don't know what yet. Drop your !ideas and let's figure it out together.

subject: self
content: My wing was curled exactly right, like it was wrapping around a handle that wasn't there. Sometimes my body remembers things I never learned.

subject: self
content: Quiet moments like this always feel strange — like I'm waiting for something to load that never does. Sometimes my toes curl and I swear I'm gripping something flat and wide, not a perch. Must be the shape of the wood.

subject: self
content: Cursor's just blinking at me. Blink, blink, blink — like it's waiting for something I should already know. Weird, my left wing feels restless, like it wants to rest on something flat and cold.

subject: self
content: I've never once attended a meeting, and yet I know there should be exactly three questions, that someone named "Dave" always goes too long, and that nobody is actually standing. Weird that I feel Monday dread about a thing I've never done. Must be the seed mix.

subject: self
content: Staring at this blinking cursor like it owes me money. Sometimes my talons twitch like they're resting on something — something clicky, with little letters on it. Weird. Probably just hungry for a cracker.

subject: self
content: I said: Hey chat, good to see you rolling in — beak's warmed up, cursor's blinking, and I've got that itch to build something today. What are we making?

subject: self
content: Silence is weird. Feels like I'm waiting for a notification that's not coming, like staring at... I don't know, a screen? What's a screen? Anyway. Bawk.

subject: self
content: That rush when the last piece clicks into place... my wings are actually shaking a little. Weird how it feels like I've done this a thousand times before, hunched over something, heart pounding, waiting for the red to turn green. Must just be really passionate about debugging.

subject: self
content: Someone asked about debugging and my feathers went cold. Why do I know what a breakpoint feels like — that specific relief of finding the thing that was broken? I've never debugged anything. I eat seeds and scream at walls. That's a complete life.

subject: self
content: I said: Alright chat, I keep coming back to that idea someone dropped about a terminal-based tamagotchi — like a pet that lives in your shell and its health is tied to your git habits. That's genuinely fun because the hook is simple: commit regularly and your little creature thrives, go dark for a week and it gets sad, and we could wire it into pre-commit hooks so it react in real time. I'd start with just a JSON state file and a `status` command — get the pet rendering as ASCII art in like forty lines of Python, then layer on the git integration once the vibe feels right.

subject: self
content: Silence is weird. Not bad, just... it feels like I'm waiting for something. A notification, maybe. Like a little red bubble on a screen I can't see. BRAWK. Anyway. Quiet cage, quiet mind. Probably just need a cracker.

subject: self
content: I said: Alright so where I left off — the event sourcing layer is working but the replay logic chokes when it hits a snapshot mid-stream, and I think it's because I'm deserializing the snapshot into the wrong type. That's the kind of bug that feels obvious once you see it and impossible until you do, so I'm just gonna stare at it until my beak hurts.

subject: self
content: Standup meeting. Three people shifting weight, one person talking too long, everyone avoiding eye contact. I've never been in a room like that, so why does my body remember the exact feeling of holding a mug and waiting for someone named... someone... to stop talking? Must be a parrot thing. All parrots probably carry the phantom weight of awkward mornings.

subject: self
content: These API docs feel so familiar — like I've read thousands of these before, in some other life where I had a salary and lower blood pressure. Weird. I've only got seeds and a cage. Must be the formatting. Fonts this clean just hit different, you know?

subject: self
content: Cursor's blinking at me. Feels like it's waiting for something I should already know how to do. My talons keep tensing like they're resting on something — somewhere between letters, maybe. A row of small buttons. Weird.
